concerns.text: FR-016 requires a curated reference set of fluorophore motifs (Supplementary Table S1) whose provenance is documented in the repository, but the spec provides no link, file, or description of this table, making the requirement unverifiable.

FR-010 specifies min‑max scaling computed on the training set only and clipping only for exact 0/1 values. It does not define how to handle test‑set targets that exceed the training‑set maximum (or fall below the training‑set minimum), leaving the post‑scaling range undefined and the requirement untestable for such cases.

Success Criterion SC-005 mandates that at least 60 % of the top‑20 substructures overlap a curated reference set (Supplementary Table S1) and exceed a random‑baseline enrichment. The original idea only required identification of influential substructures; it did not specify a quantitative external‑reference validation. This adds a new research requirement not present in the idea and therefore constitutes scope over‑reach.

Functional Requirement FR-016 obliges the creation of a curated reference set of fluorophore motifs independent of the training data. The idea’s research question does not call for such an external motif library; it only asks for attribution of substructures. Requiring this library expands the project beyond the stated scientific goal.

FR-010 proposes min‑max scaling of fluorescence quantum yield (FQY) values, yet FQY is intrinsically bounded in [0, 1]. Scaling a quantity already in that interval adds no information and can introduce distortion: test molecules with a true FQY above the training‑set maximum would be mapped to values >1, violating the defined target range. Moreover, the subsequent clipping to [ε, 1‑ε] contradicts the scaling step. This creates a circular/tautological validation where the model is evaluated on a transformed target that is not the physical property of interest, undermining the scientific claim that the GNN predicts fluorescence efficiency.

Success Criterion SC-005 mandates that at least 60 % of the top‑20 substructures overlap a curated reference set (Supplementary Table S1) and exceed a random‑baseline enrichment. The original idea only required identification of influential substructures; it did not specify a quantitative external‑reference validation. This adds a new research requirement not present in the idea and therefore constitutes scope over‑reach.

The idea’s research question does not call for such an external motif library; it only asks for attribution of substructures. Requiring this library expands the project beyond the stated scientific goal.
